entries.scope: Evaluating Yices 2 as a QF_LRA reference solver, prompted by the question of whether it is a better reference for some families than z3. Two further findings fell out: yices cannot read YinYang mutants at all without help, and for one family YinYang's mutants are ill-formed.

environment.host: workstation for the seed/generator measurements; llm2smt-slurm for the mutant scan
environment.binary: build/primo at c29ed09, z3 5.0.0, Yices 2.7.0 (x86_64 static-gmp, GPLv3, reference-only)

summary.is_yices_a_better_reference: For some families, measurably yes. At 60s z3 answers neither latendresse seed nor miplib_pp08a-9000; yices answers all three (15.9s, 15.1s, 4.7s). At the 20s mutation timeout yices oracles 29 of 34 corpus seeds against z3's 26, and its failures are a strict subset of z3's, so the union is also 29. It does not subsume z3 -- both time out on LassoRanker at 20s (yices needs 109s; primo 3s) and neither answers tropical-matrix -- so it is added as a second reference, not a replacement.
summary.generator_side: On 150 wide-coefficient FuzzSMT cases yices agreed with z3 on all 150 and ran 6x faster (0.3s against 1.9s), so it is also the cheaper generator reference.
summary.yices_cannot_read_mutants: yices-smt2 requires (set-logic ...) before Real is a defined sort and has no --logic flag; z3 infers a default. typefuzz strips the command -- 0 of 200 sampled mutants had one -- so yices failed every mutant at line 1 with 'undefined sort: Real'. As a third target it contributed nothing while still costing a process launch per mutant, visible as YinYang's effective-call rate dropping from 65.1% (job 118548 opfuzz) to 42.8% (job 118611 opfuzz). Solving eff = effective/total for the third target gives roughly zero, which is what pointed at rejection rather than timeout. Fixed by scripts/yices_smt2_ref.sh, which prepends the logic only when absent.
summary.typefuzz_mutants_are_ill_formed_for_ezsm: SUPERSEDED by the entry 2026-08-02-qf-lra-mutation-yield-is-structurally-low. The first diagnosis here -- that typefuzz invents symbols out of paren-bearing quoted names, affecting only the 2 ezsmt seeds -- was wrong on both the mechanism and the scale.

caveats: The eff comparison 65.1% -> 42.8% confounds two changes made at once: the third target AND opfuzz iterations 300 -> 200. It is not a clean measurement of yices's effect. It was still enough to point at the real defect, which was then confirmed directly by running yices on a mutant.

A prediction stated in advance -- that adding yices would raise the effective-call rate above the 28-43% band -- was wrong, and wrong for a reason worth keeping: the addition was broken, not merely unhelpful.

The ill-formed-mutant finding does NOT imply false bug reports. In opfuzz mode the first solver (primo) is the oracle; it produces no sat/unsat on these, so typefuzz counts the mutant invalid and skips it. The cost is wasted budget -- about 59 of 60 mutants for that seed -- not unsoundness.
entries.outcome: Yices added as a second reference (commit 2da20f4), wrapper added (8eac51a), gate pointed at the wrapper. Job 118611 was cancelled after its opfuzz task completed, rather than spending three more hours on the broken configuration; its opfuzz result (34/34 seeds, 0 bug triggers) stands as a primo-vs-z3 result.

entries.scope: Why YinYang mutation fuzzing yields so little against a QF_LRA-only solver. Measured directly on the mutants job 118611 left behind, after two earlier diagnoses in this log turned out to be wrong.

summary.headline: Across 25 mutants from each of 8 seed groups (200 total), Primo can answer 15 -- 7.5%. Per group: Heizmann 0/25, ezsmt 0/25, check_bignum 2/25, DTP-Scheduling 3/25, meti-tarski 4/25, miplib 1/25, sal 3/25, spider 2/25.
summary.cause_1_declaration_order: typefuzz emits declare-fun commands after their first use. Verified concretely: in a Heizmann mutant, motzkin_2059_0 is used at line 17 and declared at line 49, while in the parent seed it is declared at line 77 and first used at line 86. Primo and Yices both reject with 'unknown symbol'; z3 drops the offending assertions and answers anyway, i.e. answers a strictly weaker formula. Mechanically fixable by hoisting declarations.
summary.cause_2_nonlinearity_dominates: Hoisting is not enough: the same mutant then fails with '* requires a literal rational coefficient operand (QF_LRA)'. opfuzz and typefuzz mutate operators in a SORT-aware way, and QF_LRA's linearity is a syntactic restriction beyond sorts, so operator mutation routinely produces products of non-constant terms -- e.g. (* (+ (* motzkin_2059_0 10.0) ...) ...) -- which leave the logic. Primo correctly rejects them; z3 solves them as nonlinear.
summary.conclusion: Mutation fuzzing has a low INTRINSIC yield against a linear-arithmetic-only solver: most mutants are no longer QF_LRA. This is a property of the tool/logic pairing, not a misconfiguration, and it explains why mutation fuzzing has never found anything here. It is not unsound -- in opfuzz mode Primo is the oracle, and a mutant it cannot answer is counted invalid and skipped, so no false bug is reported. The cost is budget: roughly 13 mutants generated per usable one.

caveats: Two earlier diagnoses in this session were wrong and are corrected here. First: that typefuzz invents symbols from paren-bearing quoted names -- it does not, the symbols are declared, just later. Second: that the problem was confined to the 2 ezsmt seeds, about 6% of the corpus -- Heizmann is 0/25 and has no quoted symbols at all.

The nonlinear-product count was initially under-measured by a regex that only matched (* ident ident) on one line; the real forms are nested and multi-line. Counting shapes rather than lines is what showed it.
The seed-corpus widening is still worth having: it broadens the shapes of the ~7.5% of mutants that do stay in QF_LRA. It just does not multiply the yield the way the seed count suggests.
entries.outcome: Recorded as a structural limit rather than a defect to fix. Hoisting declarations would recover cause 1, but cause 2 dominates and has no fix short of a logic-aware mutator, so it was not implemented. Generator fuzzing (the FuzzSMT ladder) remains the higher-yield path for QF_LRA and stays the primary gate.

entries.scope: Review of the model-production merge (origin/main, 9 commits) for QF_LRA correctness and performance regressions, against the pre-merge baseline 53d3d9d.

environment.binary: build/primo at the merge vs a git-worktree Release build of 53d3d9d; baseline verified BY CONTENT (0 vs 16 produce_model refs, model_builder.cpp 1 vs 273 lines), not by --version
environment.notes: Both binaries confirmed deterministic across repeated runs; cmake configurations compared and equal.

summary.correctness: 130 files, 8 per family across all 17 division families, both builds: zero wrong answers against declared :status. Answers identical except 3 files that moved unknown -> answered, all borderline at the 20s cap and confirmed solvable by both at 40s.
summary.structural: src/theory/ is byte-identical -- the tableau and H8/H9/H10 are untouched. The merge dropped no LRA work: 37 removed lines in check_sat.cpp are all signature/constructor changes, and every LRA knob is present with identical counts. Model paths are correctly gated on options.produce_model, which is settled before solving because all commands are parsed first.
summary.defect_found: The frontend interned a term per declared Real constant at declare-fun time, assigning TermIds in declaration order rather than first-use order. Preprocessing's Gaussian elimination pivots in ascending TermId order, so this silently changed which substitutions were accepted -- unconditionally, model requested or not. On miplib/vpm2-0: :preprocessing.solve-eqs.rewrites 390 -> 252, :lra.pivots 26890 -> 12537. Fixed in e3059e6 by recording SymbolId and materialising terms after the search.
summary.post_fix_verification: Non-time statistics identical on 31 of 31 A/B instances across 11 families. Preprocessing time 1894376us vs 1893674us, ratio 0.9996 -- the unconditional substitution-trail building added by the merge costs nothing measurable.
summary.second_regression: set-option moved from silently ignored to strictly parsed, so (set-option :verbosity (- 1)) is now rejected although SMT-LIB 2.6 permits an s-expression attribute value and z3 accepts it. No file in any local corpus uses set-option, so benchmarks are unaffected. Not fixed; recorded.

caveats: Wall-clock A/B could not resolve this. Two paired runs of the same 31 instances gave ratio 0.970 (before the fix) and 1.028 (after), while the CONTROL arm -- the same baseline binary on the same files -- moved 80.80s to 84.69s between runs, a 4.8% drift. The rig's noise floor exceeds the effect size, so neither ratio is evidence. The statistics-identity comparison is what settles it.

The three unknown -> answered files were first read as the new build being faster. That comparison was confounded: the baseline sweep ran concurrently with a timing probe while the new sweep ran alone. Re-running them uncontended showed both builds solve them.
The QF_LRA UF rejection added by 095e07f is a real behaviour change, but correct per the logic definition and no division file triggers it.
entries.outcome: Merge accepted. One defect found and fixed (e3059e6) with a regression test; one narrow spec regression recorded and left; the TermId-order coupling underneath opened as a docket (docs/termid-order-sensitivity.md) with H11 proposed behind --lra-gaussian-markowitz.

entries.scope: First campaign with every piece of this session's fuzzing work active at once: the six-profile FuzzSMT ladder, QF_LRA-restricted opfuzz and typefuzz configs, --keep-logic and --hoist-declarations (now upstream in the fork at 04c8618), Yices as a second reference, and the family-complete 34-seed corpus.

environment.notes: Job 118735, 11 tasks, 6h wall. Prerequisites verified before submitting: cluster venv reinstalled via contrib/install_yinyang.py because it still predated the upstreamed flags (keep_logic reported False). Flags confirmed present in the ACTUAL command lines, not assumed from env vars.

summary.generator: 5 of 6 ladder shards complete at time of writing: 2500 cases, 2455 PASS, 45 TIMEOUT, zero wrong answers and zero REF_DISAGREEMENT. Every case consulted BOTH references -- verified from the summary CSVs as 'refs per case: {2: 2500}', since fuzz_external.py does not echo its arguments and silent reference-dropping was a real defect fixed earlier the same day.
summary.opfuzz_efficiency: The headline result. opfuzz completed all 34 seeds with 0 bug triggers at an effective-call rate of 99.7%, against 65.1% for the same task under the stock configs (job 118548) and 42.8% when Yices was added but could not read mutants (job 118611). The QF_LRA operator config plus --keep-logic is what closed it.
summary.typefuzz_efficiency: More modest: 41.7%, 65.0% and 51.3% on the three shards that ran to the wall, against a 27-43% baseline. typefuzz is generative rather than substitutional, so it produces harder mutants; the improvement is real but not the step change opfuzz saw.
summary.bug_files: 45 files under bugs/, exactly matching the 45 FuzzSMT TIMEOUTs, all in fuzzsmt shard directories and none in any mutation bugs/ directory. No defect was found anywhere in the campaign.
summary.wall_handling: Tasks 7, 8 and 10 each ran the full 10800s wall and exited 0 with 'reached the 10800s wall; this is a time-boxed run, not a failure'. Under the pre-b790e63 behaviour all three would have been recorded as FAILED.

caveats: Task 9 was SIGKILLed (exit 137) at 2:06:21 and the cause was NOT established. Memory is ruled out as the explanation: tasks 7 and 10 reported higher MaxRSS (107GB and 108GB against task 9's 80GB) on the same 2G request and completed, so those figures are an accounting artifact rather than real resident size. Primo is not reproducibly implicated -- 25 minutes and 800 mutants with primo capped at 4GB of address space produced no kill and no bug, and the largest mutant (92KB) solves in 0.01s using 9MB. Recorded as unexplained rather than attributed.
Ladder shard 0 was still running when this entry was written; its 500 cases are not included in the 2500 above.

The opfuzz and typefuzz efficiency figures are not directly comparable to each other -- opfuzz substitutes operators in place while typefuzz generates new terms -- and the local 2-target reproduction measured 76.5%, so target count moves the number too.
entries.outcome: No defect found across roughly 4700 generator and mutation cases with two independent references. The efficiency prediction stated in advance -- that the QF_LRA configs would lift the effective-call rate above the 28-43% band -- is confirmed for opfuzz (99.7%) and only partly for typefuzz (41.7-65.0%).

summary.standings_change: This revises the headline. Against z3 and cvc5 alone primo led the division by 47; with Yices included it is second. Any claim that primo leads the QF_LRA division needs the qualifier 'of the three previously compared solvers'.

Eleven of seventeen families tie exactly, ten of them saturated.
summary.complementarity: 29 instances only primo solves, 26 only Yices, 2 only z3, 3 only cvc5; 63 defeat all four. The two leaders are complementary rather than one dominating.
summary.soundness: Zero wrong answers for all four against the division's own (set-info :status), zero cross-solver disagreements, and zero benchmarks unsolved for non-standard reasons -- every unsolved instance is an honest timeout, not a parse error or refused construct.
summary.primo_unchanged: primo scores 1631 at b6b8d55 against 1631 at aa44320 (PAR2 95091 against 94992, 0.1%). Independent confirmation that the model-production merge plus today's frontend changes are behaviour-neutral on this division.

caveats: Not a single simultaneous run. primo and Yices ran 2026-08-03; z3 and cvc5 come from job 118382 on 2026-08-01 and were deliberately not re-run because neither changed. Same manifest, timeout, harness and cluster, different days.

The division desugaring committed today (57fcf0a) could in principle have changed primo's score: 146 of the 1753 files contain a syntactic (/ <non-numeral> ...). It did not -- a parse-only sweep of all 1753 files reports zero unsupported inputs both before and after, so those operands all resolve to literals through let-expansion.
No division file uses abs or set-option, so neither the abs rejection nor the set-option change affects these numbers.
entries.outcome: Cactus plot committed at docs/_static/qf-lra-cactus.svg, generated by scripts/plot_cactus.py. Yices is now the strongest solver measured on this division.

OpenSMT was run at its defaults with no flags, exactly as the other references are. No attempt was made to find a better configuration for it or for primo.

Reference-only: contrib/install_opensmt.py installs the release binary and nothing else. OpenSMT's source was not read, for the same clean-room reason stated for Yices -- its simplex core descends from the same Dutertre and de Moura paper primo's does.

summary.prototype_result: The prototype preserved the exact search and pivot counters but was slower: 6.58s, 6.73s, 6.63s wall time, max RSS about 129 MB. Reported solve-us was 6.40M, 6.54M, 6.44M.
summary.interpretation: Capacity reuse is not free in the current vector-of-pairs representation: appending the rebuilt output and erasing the old prefix adds a compaction/move pass over the same hot row data. That cost outweighed any avoided allocation on this representative pivot-heavy case.
summary.outcome: Rejected and reverted. The likely vector-level opportunity is not simple capacity reuse; any worthwhile representation change probably needs a different sparse matrix layout such as row/column linked entries or CSR-style occurrence storage, which belongs with the larger D4/revised-simplex representation work.

entries.scope: Triage of whether a respectable CSR/sparse-matrix or LP library could turn the remaining QF_LRA pivot-vector cost into a local implementation task.

environment.notes: Documentation and design triage only; no source implementation.

summary.conclusion: Tabled as a shortcut. Respectable libraries exist, but plain CSR and off-the-shelf sparse containers optimize mostly-static sparse algebra, while Primo's hot operation is a mutable exact tableau pivot that changes row length, updates a transpose occurrence view, removes zero cancellations, and must remain explainable and undoable.
summary.eigen_suitesparse: Eigen SparseMatrix and SuiteSparse are credible sparse-matrix/factorization tools, but they would not remove the need to maintain row/column synchronization, exact Rational arithmetic, strict-delta assignments, and Farkas reason extraction.
summary.highs_clp: HiGHS and CLP are the relevant respectable simplex/LP libraries, but direct use would be a solver architecture decision: numerical LP/simplex behavior would still need exact verification and SMT explanations, so this is D4-scale work rather than a container swap.
summary.what_becomes_harder_under_csr: Frequent structural row updates, deletion after coefficient cancellation, cheap column access for occurs_in_/sparse pricing/update propagation, SOI/pivot undo, and exact-arithmetic ownership.
summary.status: Recorded in docs/qf-lra-heuristics.md under D4. D4 itself remains open; the CSR/library shortcut is tabled.

entries.commit: 9dadfa1 (branch HEAD); culprit identified as ffaf9eb on main

environment.notes: Division runs on Slurm (119970 contended, 120072 spread over node-01/03/07 with --cpus-per-task=3); per-instance bisection local on the workstation, Release builds, deterministic across repeated runs.

result.parent_good: 4d4a185 'Add QF_LRA model printing': sat 0.93s, 11,735 pivots, twice
result.mechanism: ffaf9eb added contains_euf_predicate_atom, which counts any Bool-sorted Application OR Constant as an EUF predicate. A plain propositional variable qualifies, so the dispatch (has_equality || has_euf_predicate) && has_arithmetic flips this pure-QF_LRA file from :solver.qf-lra 1 to :solver.qf-uflra 1. Verified directly: the counters flip across exactly that commit pair.

entries.conclusion: The division regression predates this branch and belongs to main. main at 0c0843d reproduces the timeout with pivot counts in the same regime as HEAD (1.09M vs 1.14M) while b6b8d55 solves in 0.20s, so the branch is not the cause. The mechanism is the dispatch trigger already recorded as open-leads lead 2b, whose 'performance-neutral' verdict was measured on the stratified sample at 15s and does NOT hold on the full division at 300s. CAVEAT: this explains the 12 2019-ezsmt losses; LassoRanker (40 losses) reports :solver.qf-lra 1, the pure path, and is NOT explained by this -- tracked separately.
entries.process_notes: Two wrong turns worth recording. (1) The first division run put 67 tasks on one 56-core node; the contention hypothesis was stated too confidently and re-running with --cpus-per-task=3 moved the result by only 4 files, so contention was not the cause. (2) The first bisect script omitted --quiet and read the version banner instead of the answer, so every commit tested 'bad' and it converged on a docs-only commit. Both were caught before being reported as conclusions, but each was the first draft.

entries.process_notes: The first two LassoRanker bisections were invalid and both converged on a docs-only commit. Cause: main contains merge commits from the Nelson-Oppen branch, and that branch's own history predates QF_LRA support, so those commits answer 'unsupported logic: QF_LRA'. The script marked them bad instead of skipping. Fixed by skipping on 'unsupported'/no-answer AND bisecting with --first-parent so only mainline states are tested.

All 16 gains are LassoRanker, the family main regressed hardest on. Separately confirmed: main has lost 59 net files against b6b8d55 (gained 2, lost 61), which is the regression bisected to the Nelson-Oppen merge (84336a2) and, for 2019-ezsmt, to ffaf9eb's dispatch flip. Zero wrong answers in all three runs, on a corpus that carries (set-info :status).

entries.scope: Prototype and measure the Mechanism A fix from docs/nelson-oppen-qf-lra-regression.md: restrict has_euf_predicate to a Bool-sorted Application so a plain propositional variable no longer routes a QF_LRA formula to solve_qf_uf_lra.
entries.commit: ac7acce plus a one-line prototype patch (not committed)

environment.notes: Baseline and prototype built from the SAME commit in separate worktrees, differing only in that predicate -- verified by diff. Earlier binaries could not be trusted for this because their baked git revision strings were stale and '-dirty'.

result.worst_regression: 2019-ezsmt/routingMax/SCC_strong/p50.56: 0.23s (mixed) -> 13.01s (pure). Still SAT, so a slowdown rather than a capability loss.
result.boolean_shape_cases: propositional vars and a nested Bool equality both move to qf-lra with unchanged answers; a genuine Bool-sorted application (f x) correctly stays on qf-uflra; true/false literals unaffected (TermKind::BoolValue is distinct from Constant).

entries.conclusion: The routing fix is one line and sound on this sample (0 disagreements of 150), and it removes the pathological case worth 39.4M merges. It is NOT an unambiguous speedup: 43% of files change solver, the distribution is two-tailed (p10 0.46, p90 1.04), and one file is 56x slower on the pure path -- which is lead 2b's 'neither path dominates' showing up again. A 150-file random sample at 10s is the wrong instrument; promote only on a full-division run reporting gained/lost per family.
entries.correction: A 'second over-trigger' claimed in an earlier version of the note -- that a Bool equality sets has_equality and routes the same way -- was measured and does NOT exist. Bool-sorted equalities are rewritten during preprocessing before summarize_formula_features runs, so no Equality node over Bool reaches the dispatch. has_euf_predicate on a Bool Constant is therefore the single trigger.

entries.scope: WRONG ANSWER found while checking the proposed dispatch change: congruence is dropped for Bool-sorted uninterpreted function arguments.
entries.commit: 0c0843d (main) and b6b8d55 -- present in both, long-standing

environment.notes: Release builds; deterministic over repeated runs; z3 from contrib/local as reference.

result.reproducer: (set-logic QF_UF)(declare-fun p () Bool)(declare-fun q () Bool)(declare-fun f (Bool) Bool)(assert (= p q))(assert (not (= (f p) (f q))))(check-sat)
result.not_an_euf_bug: Adding an uninterpreted sort to force :solver.qf-uf gives the correct unsat, so EUF handles Bool arguments correctly when it runs.
result.cause: Two behaviours compose. (1) Bool-sorted equalities are rewritten during preprocessing before summarize_formula_features, so has_equality is false when every equality is over Bool. (2) The QF_UF dispatch keys ONLY on has_equality; has_euf_predicate is computed but not consulted there. The formula therefore reaches solve_boolean_conjunction, which abstracts (f p) and (f q) to independent propositional variables with no congruence rule.

entries.conclusion: A documented-as-supported feature (architecture.md: 'QF_UF inputs may pass Boolean formulas as arguments to uninterpreted functions') returns a wrong answer. Independent of the Nelson-Oppen regression and older than it. The classifier is too NARROW here -- the unsoundness direction. Fix direction: dispatch on has_application_term rather than has_equality alone, which widens what reaches solve_qf_uf and is therefore a dispatch change needing gained/lost measurement.
entries.coverage_gap: Neither fuzz gate generates this shape: FuzzSMT's QF_UF/QF_LRA invocations do not request Bool-sorted function arguments, and mutation fuzzing can only produce what the seed corpus contains -- the QF_LRA seeds have no uninterpreted functions at all.

entries.scope: Structural analysis of the tropical-matrix QF_LRA family read from the benchmark source, plus a local A/B testing whether the 468 guarded arithmetic definitions can be soundly unguarded. Establishes the encoding (tropical/arctic semiring, paired Bool -infinity flag and Real value), verifies the don't-care precondition, and measures fill-in on the one instance Primo solves. Diagnostic only; no solver change is proposed as promoted on this evidence.

environment.notes: 14 cores, load average ~2.1 during both A/B runs; the concurrent tropical propagation sweep was running but single-threaded, so contention is not a plausible explanation for a 27x gap. Local diagnostic, not a SLURM benchmark claim.

command.structure_census: grep/regex census over sandbox/non-incremental/QF_LRA/tropical-matrix/constraint-199552.smt2: 954 m/c variable pairs (36 f*, 918 l*), 468 unconditional Boolean definitions (= lKm (or lIm lJm)), 468 guarded arithmetic definitions (or lKm (= lKc (+ a b))), 0 ite, 0 multiplications.
command.dont_care_check: scratchpad guard_check2.py: inlines let bindings and walks the term with an explicit stack, treating both guard polarities (positive sibling disjunct in an or, negative sibling conjunct in an and).
command.unguarded: same binary on a rewritten copy with all 468 (or lKm (= lKc (+ a b))) replaced by (= lKc (+ a b))

result.dont_care_precondition: All 468 guarded arithmetic definitions have every occurrence of their c-variable protected by their own m-flag, so unguarding is satisfiability-preserving. 774 of 954 c-variables are fully protected; 3,774 of 5,106 occurrences (73.9%). Checking only one guard polarity reports 0 of 468 and is wrong.
result.baseline: sat in 4.13s; 15,766 decisions, 93 conflicts, 7,679 pivots, 128.4M pivot term ops.
result.unguarded: sat in 112s; 125,603 decisions, 13,359 conflicts, 526,566 pivots, 3,831M pivot term ops.
result.conclusion: Unguarding is sound (both answer sat) but 27x slower with 68x the pivots. The guards are load-bearing: setting lKm true discharges the definition at the Boolean level, so the case split is cheaper than the tableau row it avoids. This rejects the family of guard-simplifying preprocessing ideas and explains why T1 helps only because it keeps the guard.
result.fill_in: On the solved baseline run: 1,440 rows, 3,519 row-nonzeros (initial average row length 2.44), 164 rows touched per pivot, ~102 terms per row update -- roughly 42x fill-in. :lra.fixed-variables and :lra.elimination-pivots are both 0, so existing elimination machinery does nothing on this family.

artifacts.scripts: scratchpad only (guard_check2.py, unguard.py); not committed -- the note records the method and the counts, and the rewrite is a four-line regex substitution reproducible from the note.

entries.follow_up: Two leads recorded in docs/tropical-matrix-structure.md: L1, prefer m-flag variables in decision order (cheap, the Boolean layer is self-contained over 36 free inputs and the solved run shows 15,766 decisions against 93 conflicts); L2, relevancy propagation to avoid asserting theory atoms under already-satisfied guards (literature-backed, absent from Primo, needs a paper note first). Neither is implemented.

entries.scope: Local A/B of row and bidirectional row propagation layered on top of T1 (--guarded-real-equality-lowering) over all 10 tropical-matrix files, sweeping the four propagation caps. Tests whether T1's leaner CNF makes propagation pay off on the out = a + b cost rows, a combination never measured before: propagation had only been tried on the pre-T1 encoding. Rejected.

environment.notes: 14 cores; sweep ran one solver process at a time. Local diagnostic screen, not a SLURM benchmark claim. No SLURM A/B and no fuzz gate were run because nothing is promoted by this result.

command.propagation: same plus --lra-row-propagation --lra-bidirectional-row-propagation, with the four cap options at default, 128 and 1024

result.mechanism_fired: Yes: 2,088 :lra.row-propagations and 128 :lra.bidirectional-row-propagations on constraint-199552. Not a null result from code that never ran.
result.caps_not_binding: Pivots, term ops and both propagation counters are IDENTICAL at default, 128 and 1024 caps (64,272 pivots / 1,012,810,802 term ops / 2,088 / 128). Unlike the mid-band files behind D1 (fanout 521, rows of 91 terms), tropical never approaches even the default caps, so the caps were never the binding constraint.
result.cost: Against T1 alone on constraint-199552 (7,679 pivots, 128.4M term ops), propagation gives 64,272 pivots and 1,013M term ops -- 8.4x the pivots and 7.9x the term ops -- and loses the file.
result.conclusion: Rejected at every cap setting tested. Propagation is not neutral on this family, it is a regression: it loses the single file the baseline solves. Combined with the separate finding that unguarding the definitions is 27x slower (see 2026-08-04-qf-lra-tropical-matrix-structure-analysis), the encoding needs neither more propagation nor fewer guards.

entries.scope: Triage of the two leads recorded in docs/tropical-matrix-structure.md, checking whether either is already implemented before proposing work. Establishes that both are untried, that the existing --lra-theory-decisions does the opposite of L1 and is catastrophic here, and that a third and cheaper lead (L3) exists because the pure-theory-filter machinery already computes what it needs but is gated to QF_UF.

environment.notes: Single-file diagnostic on constraint-199552.smt2. Local only.

result.l1_status: Untried. --lra-theory-decisions is the nearest existing mechanism and does the inverse: cb_decide() decides arithmetic atoms first and defers Boolean flags to VSIDS.
result.l1_measurement: Baseline 3.5s sat; with --lra-theory-decisions, timeout at 90s after 9,185,550 theory decisions. A falsification test of the structural reading that came out as predicted: deciding arithmetic before the flags that make it relevant is the pathological order.
result.l2_status: Untried and genuinely absent -- no relevancy machinery in src/. The only adjacent thing is the polarity-based pure-theory-filter, which is L3.
result.l3_finding: On constraint-199552: :euf.theory-atoms 3846, :euf.pure-atoms.positive 2892 (75%), :euf.pure-atoms.negative 0, :euf.pure-filter.enabled 0, :euf.pure-literals.filtered 0. The polarity analysis runs and finds three quarters of theory atoms pure-positive, then filters none, because the mechanism is implemented for QF_UF only. Ablation confirms inertness: --pure-theory-filter=on 4.152s vs off 4.150s.

entries.follow_up: Ranked L3 (extend pure-theory-filter to LRA; cheapest, machinery already computes the answer), then L1 (invert the cb_decide filter; small, with --lra-theory-decisions as a ready-made control), then L2 (dynamic relevancy propagation; largest, needs a paper note first and should follow L3's outcome).

entries.scope: Applicability screen for monotone (one-sided) real-variable elimination across eight QF_LRA families, using the new scripts/analyze_smt2.py. Supersedes an earlier regex screen whose counts were artifacts.

environment.notes: Static analysis of benchmark files; no solver run involved.

result.one_sided_reals: latendresse 0/1708, miplib 0/996, uart 0/171, sc 0/128, DTP-Scheduling 1/11, clock_synchro 0/210, tta_startup 0/104, tropical-matrix 0/4552.
result.conclusion: Rejected on applicability. Monotone elimination is sound -- Fourier-Motzkin on a single-sign variable generates no new constraints -- but there is essentially nothing to eliminate in these families.
result.supersedes: An earlier regex screen reported 456 of 996 danoint-166 reals as one-sided. That was an artifact of matching only flat atoms and skipping nested arithmetic such as (<= (+ (* 2 x) y) 5); the correct answer is 0. The retraction is why the analyzer was written.
result.incidental_validation: The analyzer independently reproduces two previously hand-derived figures: 774 guard-protected reals on tropical-matrix/constraint-199552, and the recorded 70-72% unary/two-variable census (1,611 of 2,250, 71.6%). It also confirms the tropical don't-care structure is family-wide, not instance-specific: 3,972 of 4,552 reals guard-protected on a second, larger file.
result.known_limitation: Several families still report opaque atoms (latendresse 899, miplib 248, clock_synchro 204, tta_startup 200, sc 50). Opaque forces the conservative classification, so conclusions stay sound, but those constructs are worth identifying before the analyzer is relied on for finer questions.

entries.follow_up: Lead closed in docs/open-leads.md. The analyzer is committed at scripts/analyze_smt2.py with a --selftest covering both retracted grep errors.

entries.scope: Corpus-wide one-sided (monotone) variable screen over the entire local QF_LRA benchmark set, run to check a lead that had been closed on a sample of one file per family. The corpus contradicts the sample: the lead is reopened.

environment.notes: 14 cores, 30GB RAM. 6 parallel workers, 180s per-file timeout, 6144MB RSS cap per worker. Static analysis only; no solver was run.

result.coverage: 1753 of 1753 files analyzed successfully. Zero timeouts, zero OOMs, zero parse failures. Slowest file 43.15s against the 180s cap, so no file was excluded and the denominator is complete.
result.headline: 86,126 one-sided reals out of 4,756,176 (1.8%) corpus-wide. This contradicts the earlier 8-file screen, which found essentially none and on which the lead had been closed.
result.mechanism: The one-sided variables in 2017-Heizmann are named motzkin_*: Farkas/Motzkin multipliers from constraint-based invariant synthesis, non-negative by construction and therefore one-directional. LassoRanker is the same lineage (ranking-function synthesis via Farkas' lemma), consistent with its 85,120. This is a structural feature of how those benchmarks are generated, not incidental.
result.opaque_caveat: Overall opaque-atom rate 0.2%, but concentrated: sc 20.8% (all 144 files) and tta_startup 12.1% (all 72 files), from ite inside arithmetic terms. For those two families a zero one-sided count means the analyzer could not tell, not that none exist. Every other family is at 0.0%.
result.analyzer_fixes_this_run: Handling (* (- 1) x) via a new const_value() ground-term evaluator removed the great majority of opaque atoms corpus-wide (latendresse's first file: 899 opaque -> 0). Separately, ite_count was undercounting because the traversal stops at atom boundaries; sc actually has 380 ites per file and tta_startup 854, where the report previously said 0.

entries.follow_up: Lead reopened as entry 9 in docs/open-leads.md with a falsifier: implement detection only, report :preprocessing.monotone-eliminable on LassoRanker and Heizmann, and check it against :lra.rows / :lra.row-nonzeros. If eliminating those columns does not reduce rows or fill-in, the lead closes on solver counters rather than on a syntactic census. Separate performance follow-up recorded in the analyzer docstring: inline_lets materialises the let-DAG into a tree, which is what makes the largest files slow (~43s, ~1GB); traversing the DAG directly needs a memo key of (node, polarity, guards), never node alone.

entries.scope: External prototype of monotone (one-sided) variable elimination, to answer whether the reopened lead is worth implementing in the solver. Folds every atom mentioning a one-sided real to the constant its own polarity requires, then measures Primo before and after.

environment.notes: Prototype transformer lives in the session scratchpad and is not committed; it inlines lets and does no model reconstruction, so it is a measurement device, not a candidate implementation.

command.soundness: z3 on original vs transformed, 24 files with a one-sided population and zero opaque atoms, 20s cap
command.measurement: build/primo --quiet --stats on original vs transformed, 90s cap

result.interpretation: The saving is mostly Boolean, not tableau. The LassoRanker file folds only 21 atoms and reduces no rows at all, yet is 36% faster -- a smaller Boolean structure yields a better search. Small meti-tarski files are discharged entirely (:sat.clauses to 0) but already solve instantly, so they are not evidence of value.
result.falsifier_correction: The lead's previously stated falsifier -- close it if rows/fill-in do not drop -- is the WRONG test and would have closed a lead that works. Judge on end-to-end time and :sat.clauses instead.

entries.follow_up: Lead 9 in docs/open-leads.md updated with the measurements and a revised effort estimate. Detection and rewrite are small; model reconstruction for eliminated variables is the real work (Primo emits models, and an eliminated variable must be valued after the rest of the model from its discharged constraints, in dependency order). A Slurm fuzz gate is mandatory as this changes preprocessing.

entries.scope: Tests lead 1 in docs/open-leads.md -- extending --pure-theory-filter to LRA atoms -- by applying the change and measuring, rather than reasoning from counter names. Downgrades the lead and corrects two errors in its stated evidence. CORRECTED 2026-08-05: the first version of this entry recorded a measurement taken on a code path these files do not execute.

environment.binary: build/primo Release, with a temporary two-line change reverted afterwards
environment.notes: Diagnostic only; no committed behaviour change.

command.code_reading: src/smt/check_sat.cpp: should_filter_assignment, the two assigned_atoms_from_backend overloads, and the five LRA sites that skip on atom.filtered
command.experiment: passed options.pure_theory_filter at the two solve_qf_lra_impl call sites, rebuilt, and compared --pure-theory-filter=off against =auto on tropical-matrix/constraint-199552.smt2

result.correction_1: The filter is NOT 'QF_UF only'. The rule needs only occurs_positive/occurs_negative and the LRA side already consumes it -- five sites skip on !prepared_atom.is_arithmetic || atom.filtered. The QF_LRA path calls the two-argument assigned_atoms_from_backend overload, which hardcodes PureTheoryFilterMode::Off. A documented scope decision, not a bug.
result.correction_2: SUPERSEDED. The original text claimed the 2,892 pure-positive figure overstates the opportunity because such atoms are mostly assigned true. The supporting measurement was invalid -- it patched solve_qf_lra_impl, but these files run solve_qf_uf_lra (:solver.qf-uflra 1, :solver.qf-lra 0), so the patch was inert and the identical counters proved nothing.
result.measurement: With the two-line change applied, --pure-theory-filter=off and =auto give IDENTICAL counters on constraint-199552: 7,679 pivots and 128,402,240 pivot term ops. The filter finds nothing to do on the file that motivated the lead.
result.misleading_stats: ':euf.pure-filter.enabled' and ':euf.pure-literals.filtered' are set inside solve_qf_uf, so both read 0 on any QF_LRA file regardless of the mechanism's behaviour. That is what made the original reading look confirmed.
result.verdict: Lead downgraded, but for a different and more useful reason than first recorded. To matter, the filter must reach the online propagator's assertion path -- a materially larger change that belongs with lead 5 (relevancy propagation), since both are then about not asserting atoms during search.
result.corrected_measurement: Redone at the live call site (assigned_atoms_from_backend for lra_atoms inside solve_qf_uf_lra) with a temporary probe: of 2,892 LRA atoms, 1,177 (41%) are filtered with --pure-theory-filter=auto and 0 with =off. So the atoms ARE assigned against their polarity and the filter DOES fire hard -- and :lra.pivots (7,679) and :lra.pivot-term-ops (128,402,240) are identical either way.
result.actual_reason: ':lra.theory-checks 1' against ':lra.online-check-calls 6528'. Wiring the filter at assigned_atoms_from_backend reaches only the final check, which runs once; all 7,679 pivots happen in the online propagator, which never consults 'filtered'. The cheap version of the lead is worthless by construction rather than by accident of this benchmark.

entries.follow_up: Lead 2 (flag-first decision ordering) is top of docs/open-leads.md. Lead 1 merges into lead 5. Inverting cb_decide's is_arithmetic filter would therefore yield an EMPTY candidate set and disable theory decisions rather than reorder them. The flags are the 954 euf_atoms -- Bool-sorted Constant terms -- split off by is_euf_theory_atom.

Making the Boolean flags observed by the LRA propagator changes which callbacks CaDiCaL delivers and is a theory-combination decision, so the work belongs on the combination layer where MixedTheoryPropagationDispatcher already sees both atom sets.

entries.scope: Why pure QF_LRA benchmarks route through solve_qf_uf_lra, and what happens if they do not. Prompted by the observation that Nelson-Oppen should not fire at all on a formula with no uninterpreted content.

environment.binary: build/primo Release, with a temporary one-line experiment that was reverted

command.experiment: restricted has_euf_predicate to TermKind::Application (dropping bare Bool Constant), rebuilt, re-ran tropical-matrix/constraint-199552
command.dispatch_census: ran 40 files of benchmarks/qf-lra-stratified-sample.txt and read :solver.qf-lra / :solver.qf-uflra

result.root_cause: has_euf_predicate is set by `(kind == Application || kind == Constant) && sort == Bool`. A bare Boolean Constant -- an ordinary propositional variable -- therefore counts as an EUF predicate, and line 9108's `(has_equality || has_euf_predicate) && has_arithmetic` dispatches the formula to solve_qf_uf_lra. constraint-199552 declares no sorts and no uninterpreted functions at all: it is pure QF_LRA plus propositional variables.
result.cost_of_the_misclassification: On tropical it builds a congruence closure over the 954 Boolean constants: :euf.incremental.terms 956, :euf.incremental.merges 954. Nelson-Oppen itself no-ops (no shared real terms, :no.purification.skipped-no-sites 1).
result.SURPRISE: Routing the file to the pure QF_LRA solver instead is DRASTICALLY WORSE, not better. With has_euf_predicate restricted to Application: :solver.qf-lra 1, :euf.incremental.merges 0, and the file TIMES OUT at 180s having done 230,163 pivots. The default QF_UFLRA path solves it in 4.39s with 7,679 pivots. That is a 40x-plus regression from 'fixing' the classification.
result.dispatch_census: 14 of 40 sampled stratified-sample files (35%) take the QF_UFLRA path; 25 take the pure QF_LRA path.
result.interpretation: The misclassification is not overhead being paid for nothing -- it is load-bearing on at least one family. The 954 merges are a trivial one-time cost, and something about the QF_UFLRA solve loop is worth far more than that on this shape. Why the leaner path is 40x worse is now the open question, and it is a question about Primo's own QF_LRA solver rather than about theory combination.
result.localisation: Localised at a 60s budget, same file and options. Identical: :sat.clauses 10,059, :lra.rows 1,440, :lra.tableau-vars 2,394. Divergent: :sat.conflicts 5,256 vs 93, :sat.decisions 59,388 vs 15,766, :lra.online-check-calls 58,146 vs 6,528, :lra.pivots 98,191 vs 7,679. Preprocessing, clausification and tableau construction agree exactly; the entire divergence is in search.
result.ruled_out: NOT the observed-variable set. solve_qf_lra observes all 3,846 theory atoms while solve_qf_uf_lra observes only the 2,892 arithmetic ones, which looked like the obvious cause. Restricting the pure path to observe only arithmetic atoms does not help: still a 180s timeout, at 307,336 pivots, slightly worse. Also NOT Nelson-Oppen doing useful work -- it no-ops for lack of shared real terms.

entries.follow_up: Filed as a TODO in docs/open-leads.md rather than fixed, on instruction: Nelson-Oppen is heavily under construction in another branch and this sits in solve_qf_uf_lra and the dispatch, both of which that work touches. Two paths producing identical encodings and wildly different searches is a behaviour bug regardless of which is faster; the goal is convergence, and 'always assume NO' is a legitimate route since on a single theory the combination layer should reduce to nothing. The remaining check is to diff the two solve LOOPS, not their setup, which is already known to agree.

entries.scope: Whether the two QF_LRA solve paths differ systematically or just chaotically. Settles the claim in an earlier entry that their divergence is a behaviour bug -- it is not.

environment.binary: two builds differing only in the has_euf_predicate line: /tmp/primo-mixed (Bool Constant counts, current default) and /tmp/primo-pure (Application only). Both from dfb83f8; neither change is committed.
environment.notes: 15s per file. Local because the question is a direction check across many small runs, not a headline benchmark claim.

command.selection: every stratified-sample file whose dispatch actually differs: has a Bool 0-ary constant, no uninterpreted function, no declared sort -- 130 of 237
command.driver: scratchpad pathcmp.sh, timing both builds per file

result.tally: comparable 80 (62%), both timeout 21, pure faster 19 (1.5-7.6x), mixed faster 6 (2.2-55.2x), pure solves where mixed times out 2, mixed solves where pure times out 2.
result.verdict: Neither path dominates. Timeout wins are exactly even at 2-2, and where the paths differ the pure path is faster more often. The divergence is chaotic, as expected from a search perturbation in CDCL(T), not systematic.
result.supersedes: The earlier entry 2026-08-05-qf-lra-boolean-constant-dispatch-finding called this a behaviour bug on the strength of a single 40x instance. That framing was an overclaim from n=1 and is retracted; the 40x is one draw from a two-tailed distribution.

entries.follow_up: Design decision recorded in docs/open-leads.md: KEEP the dedicated LRA-only solver without Nelson-Oppen, since on a single theory the combination layer has nothing to do. What is recorded instead is the hazard -- dispatch is a nondeterminism trigger. Adding one (declare-fun p () Bool) to a pure QF_LRA problem changes which solver runs and can change runtime by an order of magnitude either way, so benchmark results are not comparable across an edit that adds or removes a Boolean constant, performance reports should name :solver.qf-lra vs :solver.qf-uflra, and mutation-fuzzer timing data is not meaningful (answers still are).

entries.scope: Where LRA time actually goes, to settle lead 7 (row representation: sorted arrays of pairs versus hash tables, per Griggio thesis 2.5.2) with a profile rather than a transplanted benchmark number.

environment.notes: perf is unavailable in this sandbox (kernel.perf_event_paranoid = 4, 'Failure to open any events'); callgrind was started and abandoned once gprof answered the question.

command.instance: tropical-matrix/constraint-199552.smt2: 7,679 pivots, 1,260,035 pivot row updates, 128.4M pivot term ops

result.flat_profile: LraTableau::pivot 74.08% self (2.83s of 3.82s, 7,679 calls, 0.37ms/call); Rational::operator* 12.04% (48.1M calls); Rational::from_int128_reduced 3.93% (83.0M calls); Rational::operator+ 2.88% (34.8M calls); LraTableau::update 2.09%; Rational copy constructor 1.05% (53.6M calls); CaDiCaL internals about 2% in total.
result.aggregate: pivot plus rational arithmetic is roughly 94% of runtime: 74% in pivot's own merge loop and 20% in rational operations.
result.answers_lead_7: There is NO hash or map cost in the LRA hot path at all. The only hashtable entries in the profile are TermPairKey lookups (Nelson-Oppen interface equalities) at 0.00%. Primo's Row is already std::vector<std::pair<LraVarId, Rational>> kept ordered by var id -- the sorted-array-of-pairs design the thesis endorses -- with lower_bound for coefficient lookup and a linear two-way merge for combination (item H8). The thesis's 1.20x for choosing wrongly is therefore already banked, and the class comment records that rows_ WAS std::unordered_map and was migrated away for exactly this reason.
result.what_the_profile_points_at_instead: Term-operation volume and rational cost, not the container. 83.0M from_int128_reduced calls against 48.1M multiplies means roughly 1.7 normalisations per multiply, and 53.6M Rational copies is a large number for 1.26M row updates. Reducing fill-in (fewer terms) or making the small-rational path cheaper are the levers this profile supports.

entries.follow_up: Lead 7 closed as already-implemented, on profile evidence rather than on a code read alone. Also fixed a stale comment in select_entering_variable that claimed 'Row isn't sorted by var id', contradicting the Row invariant that pivot()'s merge depends on.

entries.scope: Measures the cost of the linear occurs_in_ removal inside LraTableau::pivot, after a gprof profile put pivot at 74% self time with rational arithmetic separately accounted for. Answers whether the erase/remove scan is rare bookkeeping or a dominant cost.

environment.binary: build/primo Release with three temporary counters, reverted afterwards

command.probe: counted occurs_in entries iterated per pivot, calls to the erase/remove in the cancellation branch, and the total elements those scans touched

result.iterated: 1,260,035 occurs_in entries iterated in total (this is the Markowitz factor, |occurs_in(entering)| summed over pivots)
result.erase_calls: 12,033,307 -- about 9.5 removals per pivot row update, i.e. roughly TEN TIMES more removals than iterations
result.erase_scanned: 8,174,083,067 elements scanned by those removals; average occurrence-list length 679
result.magnitude: 8.17 billion scanned elements against 128.4M pivot term ops -- 64x more work in the bookkeeping than in the arithmetic it maintains. At a generous 4 elements/ns that is about 2.0s of pure scanning in a 4.4s solve, consistent with pivot's 74% self time and with Rational copies being only 1.05%.
result.correction: An earlier reading of this code claimed removals were rare, taken from the comment 'This is the *only* removal the loop performs' -- which says WHICH removal, not how often. The measurement says the opposite.

entries.follow_up: Filed as a lead in docs/open-leads.md. The container question is now settled by data rather than by the general principle that vectors iterate better than hash sets: iteration is 6,500x cheaper than the removal scans here, so almost any structure with sub-linear removal wins, even one with slower iteration.

entries.scope: Prototype of lead 3b candidate 3: replace occurs_in_'s per-variable std::vector with std::unordered_set so removal is O(1), including the requested initial-capacity (reserve) variants. Also establishes that the cancellation rate generalises beyond tropical-matrix.

environment.binary: four builds from the same tree: baseline, unordered_set with no reserve, and with per-variable reserve(8) and reserve(32). All prototypes reverted; nothing committed.

command.cancellation_census: temporary counters on both occurs_in_ erase sites, across five families
command.ab: same instance through each build, comparing wall time and :lra.pivots

result.cancellation_generalises: Cancellation is NOT tropical-specific: 9.4% of merged terms on tropical constraint-199552, 13.8% latendresse ecoli, 18.0% miplib danoint-166, 12.1% uart-16, 9.5% sc-21. Scanned-elements-per-merged-term ranges 6x to 64x.
result.search_unchanged: :lra.pivots is IDENTICAL between baseline and prototype on every instance measured (7,679 / 3,654 / 847 / 282,354), so unordered_set's different iteration order does not perturb pivot selection and the timings measure container cost cleanly rather than a search change.
result.the_deciding_factor: AVERAGE OCCURRENCE-LIST LENGTH, not total elements scanned. danoint-166 scans 1.8x MORE elements in total than tropical (14.6B vs 8.2B) and gets 19% WORSE, because its average list is 76 against tropical's 679. The vector scan is contiguous, vectorisable and cache-friendly, so it is very cheap per element; a hash erase costs a hash plus a probe plus a likely cache miss regardless of list length. Hashing only wins once the list is long enough to amortise that. Crossover is somewhere between 76 and 679.
result.reserve_result: The requested initial-capacity setting makes things WORSE, not better: on tropical, no-reserve 3.20s against reserve(8) 3.50s and reserve(32) 3.38s. Reserving per variable pays allocation and memory for every variable, and most occurrence lists are short.
result.model_correction: The framing that '8.17 billion scanned elements must be the bottleneck' was too simple. Removing the scans entirely on tropical wins 25%, not the ~45% a 2.0s-of-4.4s estimate implied, which means contiguous scanning is substantially faster per element than that estimate assumed.

entries.follow_up: Candidate 3 (unordered_set) is rejected as a blanket change: it is a regression on three of five instances including the largest. What survives is the diagnosis -- long occurrence lists are expensive to maintain -- and the two untried candidates, tombstone/superset and swap-and-pop with a position index, both of which keep contiguous iteration. A length-triggered hybrid is also now suggested by the data.

entries.scope: Second prototype for lead 3b (swap-and-pop with a position index), plus the occurrence-list length histogram that explains where the scan cost actually lives and suggests it may be predictable from the formula.

environment.binary: builds from the same tree: baseline, unordered_set, swap-and-pop with an unordered_map position index. All prototypes reverted; nothing committed.

result.histogram: At each cancellation erase on tropical constraint-199552 (12.0M calls, 8.17B elements): lists under 256 account for 2.9% of scanning, 256-511 for 10.5%, 512-1023 for 51.6%, and 1024+ for 34.9%. So 86.5% of all scanning happens on lists of 512 or more -- the mean of 679 hides a heavily skewed population.
result.why: Consistent with docs/tropical-matrix-structure.md: the family is a DAG of definitions over 36 free f* variables, so pivoting composes rows back toward those few variables and their occurrence lists become enormous. The long lists follow from the formula's shape.
result.predictability_hypothesis: UNTESTED. scripts/analyze_smt2.py already recovers free-versus-derived structure and occurrence counts statically. If occurrence-length distribution correlates with a static measure, representation could be chosen per instance or per variable before search. The correlation has not been checked and that check gates any adaptive scheme.
result.swappop: tropical 4.11s -> 3.70s; sc-21 0.46 -> 0.50; uart-16 0.23 -> 0.27; latendresse 0.25 -> 0.37. Worse than the unordered_set prototype on every instance.
result.why_swappop_loses: Structural, not an implementation detail: the position index is itself a hash map, so each erase costs a hash find, a hash erase, and a hash write to repair the moved element -- two to three hash operations against unordered_set::erase's one, plus swap bookkeeping. It only wins with a non-hash index, and a dense pos_[var][basic] is O(vars^2): 23MB for tropical's 2,394 tableau variables but about 34GB for a LassoRanker instance with 92,937 reals.
result.test_gap_found: The first swap-pop version cleared occurs_in_'s vectors in rebuild_occurs_in_index without clearing the position index, leaving stale positions for a later erase to act on. All 13 unit suites passed with that bug present, so nothing currently exercises a rebuild followed by a removal.

entries.follow_up: Two of three candidates now rejected by measurement. What remains is the tombstone/superset variant, and the principled version of swap-and-pop -- the standard sparse-matrix representation with each nonzero linked into both a row and a column list, carrying its position in the row entry so no separate index exists (King's thesis Section 2.2.7). Also recorded as a prerequisite for any adaptive scheme: check whether occurrence-length distribution is predictable from static formula structure.

entries.conclusion: Yes, it costs something, and the cost has one shape. 3 of the 7 regressions over 10% are latendresse/ecoli, the family with the longest rows in the corpus (691 terms). unlink_occurrence repairs the moved entry's back-index with a std::lower_bound over that entry's ROW, so long-row instances pay O(log row) where they previously paid a short column scan -- the exact mirror of tropical's long-column win. RowEntry growing 32->40 bytes is a second candidate cause predicting the same family; narrowing LraVarId to 32 bits separates them. The principled fix is to finish the cross-link (store the row slot in occurs_in_ too), making the fixup O(1). Net today: 0 lost, worst ~10% above 1s, against tropical 1/10 -> 2/10.

entries.scope: Identify and fix the LassoRanker half of main's division regression -- 46 of the 61 lost files, which the dispatch mechanisms did not explain.

environment.notes: gprof builds (-pg -O2 -g, PRIMO_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=OFF -- the default -Werror trips a libstdc++ false positive under these flags). perf is unavailable in this sandbox.

entries.method: Ran both commits under --max-theory-conflicts 2000 so each stopped after the SAME logical work: both answered sat with 884 conflicts and 10,217 pivots, byte-identical search. That made the flat profiles directly comparable as pure constant factor, with no trajectory noise.

result.profile_b6b8d55: LraTableau::pivot 19.7%, update_violation_status 17.0%, Rational comparisons -- ordinary simplex
result.profile_main: OnlineLraPropagator::notify_backtrack 62.1% (94.97s over 9,348 calls), _Hashtable<TermPairKey,...>::_M_find_before_node 28.9% with 1,404,326,272 calls (~150k lookups per backtrack)
result.mechanism: notify_backtrack calls rebuild_true_interface_bounds() unconditionally, which rescans EVERY theory atom and hash-inserts each true one into true_lra_le_reasons_. pending_interface_equalities_ is drained only by MixedTheoryPropagationDispatcher, so on the pure QF_LRA path nothing consumes any of it -- filled on every assignment, rebuilt on every backtrack, discarded.
result.fix: interface_equalities_enabled_ defaults to false; MixedTheoryPropagationDispatcher (the only consumer) turns it on. Guards both rebuild_true_interface_bounds and observe_true_interface_bound.
result.instance_after_fix: 200s timeout -> sat in 12.16s, with 10,217 pivots and 884 conflicts -- identical to the pre-regression commit, and marginally faster than its 13.44s
result.no_path_unaffected: With --nelson-oppen-prop online on a formula where x<=y and y<=x must publish x=y to EUF, both builds give unsat with :no.online.lra-published-equalities 1 and precreated 2. Pinned by a new regression test asserting >= 1.

entries.conclusion: The LassoRanker regression is Nelson-Oppen interface-equality bookkeeping running on the pure QF_LRA path, where nothing consumes it. Gating it on the one consumer recovers the instance exactly (identical search counters to b6b8d55) and gains 6 files with 0 lost on a 120-file sample, never slower than baseline (max paired ratio 1.01). All six gains are LassoRanker. This is the third and largest of the three mechanisms in docs/nelson-oppen-qf-lra-regression.md and the one that accounts for 46 of main's 61 lost files.

The generated gate did not contain this shape, and the one-seed mutation corpus was too thin to qualify the profile for broad evaluation.
entries.outcome: Rejected as performance evidence because of wrong answers. No solved-count, PAR2, decision, or propagation difference from these jobs may support promotion. result.by_inspection: Of three src/ commits, two add const methods with NO caller (model_equal_classes, entailed_equalities). The third threads MixedDispatchMode through summarize_formula_features; under the default Narrow the expression reduces to `Application && bool_sort`, character-for-character what main computes.
result.first_sweep_explained: 16 of the 17 were files that TIME OUT, whose counters record progress-at-cutoff and vary run to run regardless of code. The 17th solves in 9.90s against the sweep's 10s cap -- straddling the cutoff. Run three times per binary at a 60s budget it is identical and deterministic on both: 29,081 pivots, 840,202 decisions, 1,451 conflicts.

entries.conclusion: Pure QF_LRA behaviour is preserved exactly: 89 of 89 commonly-solved files bit-identical on search counters, 0 answer differences anywhere. Consistent with the code, which has no path doing anything main does not.
entries.method_note: Counter comparisons across runs are only meaningful on instances that COMPLETE. A timeout is not a measurement, it is a snapshot of wherever the search had reached. This is the second time in one session that artifact produced a false alarm -- the first was the supposed node-contention regression on the full division. Restricting to completed runs is the fix; explaining the difference away is not.
